brief.title: TUV SUD Automotive Service Technician
brief.audience: Learners with zero automotive background, taken to TUV SUD certification readiness
brief.notes: An 8-week intensive program that takes a learner with zero automotive background through to TUV SUD certification readiness. Every week tells a story, every day earns the right to teach the next. The program follows a Foundation-System-Integration spiral: first show the whole car, then teach safety, then give the electrical language, then go system-by-system deeper, and finally integrate everything. Programme: 8 weeks mandatory (120 hrs) + 3 weeks optional (45 hrs). Format: 5 days/week x 3 hrs/day = 15 hrs/week. Certification: TUV SUD Automotive Service Technician. Exam: 50 MCQ (100 marks across 17 chapters). Version 4.0 (2026-03-24).

modules.title: Meet the Machine
topics: The Car — From Nose to Tail
Hazards, Compliance & the Fluids That Run Through a Car
modules.note: Automotive Fundamentals, Safety & Precision Stage: Foundation. You've never touched a car professionally. By Friday, you'll know every major system by name and location, you'll be safe to work in any workshop, and you'll measure to hundredths of a millimetre.

modules.title: Speaking Electricity
topics: Why Electronics Run the Car — E/E Architecture & ECU Concepts
Electrical Theory — Ohm's Law, Circuits & Faults
modules.note: E/E Architecture, Electrical Fundamentals & Wiring Craft Stage: Foundation. Every system you'll study from next week onwards is controlled by electronics. This week, you learn WHY electronics run the car, WHAT the electrical architecture looks like, and HOW to work with it using your hands and a multimeter.

modules.title: The Heart
topics: Air + Fuel = Combustion — The Engine's Two Inputs
Inside the Engine — Valve Train, Timing & Assembly
modules.note: Engine Systems: Air, Fuel & Combustion Stage: System Deep Dives. An engine needs exactly two things to run: air and fuel. This week starts from that simple truth. Day 1 traces how air enters the engine and how fuel gets added to it. Then we zoom in: fuel systems, ignition systems, intake details. By the end, you're inside the valve train, verifying cam timing with a dial gauge.

modules.title: Keep It Alive
modules.note: Lubrication, Cooling, Exhaust & Forced Induction Stage: System Deep Dives. Last week you built the engine in your mind. This week: what keeps it alive. Oil reduces friction. Coolant carries heat away. Exhaust removes waste gases. And if you want more power? Force more air in with a turbocharger.

modules.title: Grip, Turn & Stop
topics: Vehicle Dynamics — How Cars Grip, Turn & Stop
Brake Systems — From Pedal to Wheel
modules.note: Vehicle Dynamics, Suspension, Steering & Brakes Stage: System Deep Dives. Before we touch a single suspension component, we answer the question every driver instinctively understands: how does a car grip the road, change direction, and come to a stop? Day 1 builds physical intuition — tyres, forces, friction.

modules.title: Power Delivery & Power Supply
topics: The Power Flow — From Crankshaft to Contact Patch
modules.note: Transmission, Driveline & Starting/Charging Stage: System Deep Dives. The engine makes power. But how does that power reach the wheels? And what keeps the whole vehicle electrically alive? This week opens with the big picture — follow the power from crankshaft to tyre contact patch.

modules.title: The Future & The Comfort
modules.note: EV/Hybrid, HVAC & Vehicle Safety Systems Stage: System Deep Dives. The car of today — and tomorrow. High voltage demands new respect, climate control demands precision, and safety systems are getting smarter than ever.

modules.title: The Complete Technician
topics: CAN Bus & Network Diagnostics — Deep Dive
modules.note: Body Electronics, Networking & Cross-System Integration Stage: Integration. A real technician doesn't think in chapters. This week, you stop being a student and start thinking like a diagnostician. Every system connects through the network.

modules.title: The Craftsman
modules.note: Wiring, Welding, Body & Finishing (Optional) Stage: Optional Extension.

Reinstall the strut assembly on the vehicle and torque all fasteners to specification
Explain why wheel alignment is MANDATORY after any strut or suspension work
Remove a lower control arm following the correct fastener sequence (weight-on vs weight-off bolts)
Support the hub/knuckle assembly before disconnecting the arm to prevent brake hose and ABS sensor damage
Use a hydraulic press safely to extract worn bushes (correct mandrel selection, shielding, controlled pressure)
Press in new bushes with correct orientation (voided sections aligned per manufacturer specification)
Remove and replace a ball joint using press or staked-type methods
Explain and apply the critical concept of torquing suspension bolts at ride height
State why wheel alignment is mandatory after any suspension arm or bush replacement
Perform a gearbox function test (shift through all gears, check for noise, grinding, pop-out, and reverse engagement)
Verify suspension geometry visually (ride height, vehicle level, wheel alignment by eye)
Execute a structured road test procedure covering low-speed maneuvering, acceleration, cruising, braking, cornering, and rough-road evaluation
Listen for and identify abnormal noises and vibrations during a road test
Assess shift quality, steering feel, returnability, and brake pedal feel under real driving conditions
Document road test findings on a standardised checklist with pass/fail per system
Summarise the complete Week 10 accomplishment: gearbox strip, inspection, rebuild, strut replacement, arm and bush replacement, and final road test verification
Explain the principles of OEM harness routing — why specific routes are chosen and what hazards to avoid
Select the correct loom tape type (PVC, cloth, fleece) for a given application area
Correctly fit grommets for waterproof bulkhead panel transitions
Perform a solder splice and a crimp splice to OEM repair standards
Use terminal release tools to de-pin and re-pin connector housings without damage
Select the correct wire gauge for a repair — matching original or going one size up, never down
Plan a harness build from a pin-out diagram — identify wire count, lengths, connector types, and routing path
Cut wires to specified lengths with appropriate service loops
Crimp pin terminals onto wire ends to OEM standard (correct crimp zone, insulation grip, conductor grip)
Assemble connector shells with correctly positioned terminals and engaged secondary locks
Apply loom tape wrapping in the correct technique (half-overlap spiral) using appropriate tape type
Fit grommets at panel pass-through points
Route a completed harness on a mock-up board following a specified path
Test every circuit for continuity and every terminal for mechanical retention (tug test)
Create a pin-out diagram documenting the completed harness
Set up a MIG welding machine for mild steel — wire speed, voltage, and shielding gas flow rate
Prepare joints correctly — cleaning, fit-up, and clamping
Identify and don correct welding PPE (auto-darkening helmet, leather gloves, leather apron, safety boots)
Perform basic welding practice: butt joint, lap joint, and fillet weld in flat position
Execute a simulated exhaust repair — patch welding a hole in mild steel tubing
Inspect welds for common defects: porosity, undercut, cold lap, and incomplete penetration
Explain resistance spot welding principles and how body panels are joined at the factory
Determine when welding is appropriate vs when it is not — structural vs non-structural, insurance and certification considerations
Explain the difference between unibody (monocoque) construction and body-on-frame construction, and identify which vehicles use each
Identify exterior panels — bonnet, doors, boot lid, wings/fenders — and distinguish bolt-on panels from welded panels
Describe bumper system components (cover, absorber, reinforcement bar) and explain pedestrian protection requirements
Identify interior trim components and clip types, and demonstrate correct removal technique without damage
Explain factory corrosion protection layers (e-coat, primer, basecoat, clearcoat) and aftermarket underbody and cavity wax treatments
Inspect and replace weatherstripping — door seals and window seals
Describe the components of a car audio system: head unit, amplifier, speakers (component vs coaxial, subwoofer), and wiring (RCA, speaker wire gauge, signal vs power)

Describe basic NVH diagnostic tools (chassis stethoscope, vibration analyzer concept)
